To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mutation in a single cTnC residue (L29Q) alters the Ca(2)+ binding and release characteristics and the Ca(2) + sensitivity of force generation, and the SL dependence of force generation in cardiac myocytes.
the cardiac troponin-C mutation L29Q increases the Ca(2)-binding affinity of the regulatory site and alters Ca(2+) sensitization and length dependence of force generation in cardiac myocytes.
the L29 residue of cardiac troponin (Tn) C plays an important role, together with neighboring Asp2, Val 28 and Gly30 residues, in determining the Ca2+ affinity of site II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the structural and functional basis for the L29Q cTnC mutation and its effects on the Ca( 2+) activation of cardiac myocytes.
understanding the role of cTnI and cTnC in the regulation of myocyte contractility and the molecular mechanisms of cardiac hypertrophy and failure.
the role that mutations in cardiac troponin I, troponin T, and troponin C play in familial hypertrophic cardiop myopathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the L29 mutation, together with neighboring amino acid residues (Asp2, Val28 and Gly30), is important for determining the Ca( 2+) affinity of cTnCI, the regulation of cardiac myofilament contractile function, and the response of cardiac myofilaments to an SL change.
the L29 mutation enhances Ca(2+) affinities of site II of McTn, which in turn results in increased Ca(2+) sensitivities of force generation.

the L29 mutation, in conjunction with the D2N, V28I, and G30D mutations, results in a significant increase in Ca(2+ binding to site II of McTn, and that this results in an increase in the Ca(2) sensitivity of force generation and a reduction in the SL dependence of the Ca(2)+ sensitivity of force generation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a mutation in the Ca(2+)/Mg(2+) regulatory site of McTnT can affect Ca(2+) release, Ca(2+) sequestration, and the Ca(2) + sensitivity of force generation.
a mutation of L29 in McTnC increases the Ca(2) affinity and the rate of Ca2+ binding to site II and reduces the sensitivity of the myofilaments to changes in SL.
the L29, together the neighboring residues, Asp, Val, Gly, and Leu, plays a key role in regulating the Ca(2)+ binding characteristics of McTnI and McTnT.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the L29 mutation, in combination with the D2N mutation, alters Ca(2+) sensing and force generation in cardiac myocytes, suggesting that the L29 and D2 residues play a role in the SL-sensing mechanism.
the L29 residue plays a critical role in determining the regulatory properties of cTnCs and that mutations at this residue can alter Ca(2+) regulation and force generation in cardiac myocytes.
the L29 residue plays an important role, together with neighboring sites, in regulating Ca(2+) release from site II of McTn.
